name: Sabteca
overview: Sabteca is a male figure identified in the Bible primarily as the son of Cush. Beyond this lineage, Scripture does not provide additional details regarding his tribe or other notable attributes. His mention is brief and focused on his genealogical position.
namesAndTitles: The name Sabteca appears only once in Scripture and carries no recorded meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Sabteca is recorded as a son of Cush, establishing his place within the genealogical line descending from Noah’s son Ham. No other family relationships or descendants are noted in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Sabteca's significance lies chiefly in his role within the genealogical record found in Genesis 10:7, which traces the descendants of Cush. This genealogy is important for understanding the spread of nations and peoples after the Flood, emphasizing God's sovereign ordering of human history. While Sabteca himself is not a major biblical character, his mention contributes to the biblical framework of nations and peoples as part of God's providential plan.
